inputs.provider_selected_by: Automatic suitability analysis — all six providers evaluated

exec_summary: All six supported providers (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, IBM Cloud, Oracle Cloud, Tencent Cloud) were evaluated automatically against the stated requirements; Google Cloud ranked first with an overall suitability of 92.9/100 and was selected for the detailed analysis below.
Legacy Co is evaluated for a 'Moderate' compute workload in us-east-1, with 1000 GB of Internal-class storage and 5000 expected users.
The configured estimate on Google Cloud totals $149.60/month ($1,795.20/year) — 29.9% of the stated monthly budget.
Security posture scores 65/100 (High risk) with 0 high, 6 medium and 7 low findings across 13 domains — simulated configuration analysis, not a live scan.
All figures are estimates. Estimated pricing — verify with provider pricing calculator.

cost_drivers: Compute is the dominant driver (65% of the Google Cloud estimate): 4× e2-medium (2 vCPU / 4 GiB) at $0.0335/hr × 730 h.
Storage rates differ per provider (Azure $0.018/GB-mo vs Oracle $0.025/GB-mo) — at 1000 GB this alone moves the monthly estimate by $7.00.
Network/other is a flat 10% uplift plus a per-user baseline — real egress depends on your traffic patterns.
Cheapest configured estimate: Google Cloud ($149.60/mo); highest: IBM Cloud ($352.42/mo). Differences reflect list-price baselines, not committed-use discounts.

domains.note: Verify least-privilege IAM policies and schedule periodic access reviews.
Enable MFA for all user accounts before production rollout.
Encryption at rest by default (AES-256), CMEK via Cloud KMS — verify key policy and rotation.
TLS 1.2+ is enforced on managed endpoints — confirm custom endpoints and client configuration.
Default VPC isolation is available — validate subnet design before launch.
Enable provider firewall / security groups with deny-by-default rules; place a WAF in front of public endpoints.
Enable Security Command Center and ship platform logs to an immutable store.
Enable automated backups and test restores quarterly.
Enable provider image/workload vulnerability scanning and patch SLAs for compute workloads.
Block public access at account level; serve data through private endpoints or signed access.
Enable posture management (Security Command Center) and remediate findings on a defined SLA.
Provider-managed AES-256 is acceptable — document key ownership.
No specific framework targeted; baseline provider best practices apply.
